bug_description.normalized: The staged 2880-byte OpenType font drives HarfBuzz's shaping fallback into `hb_ot_get_glyph_extents()`, which dispatches to `OT::cff2::accelerator_t::get_extents()` and extracts an attacker-controlled CFF2 charstring. On the reproduced crash path that charstring reaches `OpCode_blendcs`; `process_blend()` loads a nonzero cached region count `k`, pops attacker-controlled blend arity `n`, and then computes `start = env.argStack.get_count() - ((k + 1) * n)` without checking that enough operands remain. Because the remaining operand count is smaller than `(k + 1) * n`, the unsigned subtraction underflows to a huge index, line 241 requests an out-of-range `BlendArg` from `argStack`, `hb_vector_t::operator[]` substitutes `Crap(BlendArg)` backed by global `_hb_CrapPool`, and `CFF::BlendArg::set_blends()` reads past that global placeholder at line 61. The staged metadata fix commit 72d8f76368b264a42fe58438fe15811d458a7935 is only the testcase addition; the actual guard is commit 14d29a10437205566c4bd7bcfa2282d34d9f4f2f.

source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed crash path that materializes vulnerability-relevant attacker data: the selected glyph's CFF2 CharString program.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 2880-byte OpenType font blob used by Stage 01. During the crashing `hb_shape()` path, fallback glyph positioning eventually requests extents for a glyph, and line 108 extracts that glyph's CFF2 charstring from the attacker-controlled `CharStrings` table. The saved ASan stack then shows this bytecode reaches `process_blend()` and `set_blends()`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `set_blends()` copies blend deltas from the caller-supplied `blends_` array, but on the crashing path that pointer aliases `_hb_CrapPool` instead of a real `BlendArg[k]` slice.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` at `src/./hb-cff2-interp-cs.hh:61:17` on an address 8 bytes to the right of global `_hb_CrapPool` defined in `hb-static.cc:42`.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable `blend` handler computes the starting operand index with unsigned subtraction but omits the required guard that the remaining stack depth is at least `(k + 1) * n`.
root_cause.note: Commit 14d29a10437205566c4bd7bcfa2282d34d9f4f2f adds `if (unlikely (env.argStack.get_count () < ((k+1) * n))) { env.set_error (); return; }` immediately before this line. Without that check, the crashing input underflows `start` to a huge index and line 241 derives an invalid `blends_` pointer from it.

parser_admitted.description: On the crashing shaping path, earlier extents providers do not return a result and HarfBuzz dispatches into the CFF2 extents interpreter. The saved crash stack includes `hb_ot_get_glyph_extents -> OT::cff2::accelerator_t::get_extents`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This pops the attacker-controlled blend arity `n` from the CFF2 operand stack. Together with `k`, it determines the required operand footprint `(k + 1) * n` used by the underflowing index calculation.

fine_trace.note: Materializes the selected glyph's attacker-controlled CFF2 charstring into `str`. This is the bytecode stream the crashing interpreter instance later dispatches through `blend`.

Initializes the CFF2 interpreter with the attacker-controlled charstring and the font-selected variation state. This binds `env.substr` to `str` and gives later `blend` handling access to the font's cached variation-store metadata.

On the crashing interpreter iteration, `fetch_op()` has just read `OpCode_blendcs` from `env.substr`, so the switch enters `process_blend()` with the operand stack already populated by earlier numeric operators from the same charstring.

Loads the cached blend-region count into local `k`. `env.process_blend()` populates that cache from the font's CFF2 variation store the first time a blend is seen and reuses it thereafter; the crashing path proves the `k` used here is nonzero because `set_blends(..., k, ...)` later executes its copy loop.

Pops the attacker-controlled blend arity `n` from the top of the CFF2 operand stack and converts it to unsigned. `n` tells `process_blend()` how many default values it expects to decorate with blend deltas.

Computes the starting index of the default-value block by subtracting the required operand footprint `(k+1)*n` from the current stack depth with unsigned arithmetic. Because the guard `env.argStack.get_count () < ((k+1) * n)` is missing here, the crashing input underflows `start` to a huge index instead of rejecting the malformed `blend`.

fine_trace.code: env.argStack[start + i].set_blends (n, i, k, &env.argStack[start + n + (i * k)]);
fine_trace.note: Uses the underflowed `start` to derive the delta base `start + n + (i * k)` and passes `&env.argStack[...]` as `blends_` into `set_blends()`. On the crashing path this source index no longer points inside the operand stack's live blend values.

The out-of-range operand-stack request from step 7 reaches `hb_vector_t::operator[]`. Because the wrapped unsigned index is far beyond the backing vector length, this operator returns `Crap(BlendArg)`, the writable placeholder backed by global `_hb_CrapPool`, so `blends_` aliases that single global object instead of a real `BlendArg[k]` array.

Treats `blends_` as a `k`-element array and copies from it into `deltas`. Because step 8 supplied `_hb_CrapPool` instead of a real delta slice, this read walks off the global placeholder and triggers the ASan global-buffer-overflow at line 61.

format.name: OpenType/CFF2 font blob
format.contract: The staged witness is the exact 2880-byte font blob in `poc`, accepted by `hb_face_create()` and later routed into `OT::cff2::accelerator_t::get_extents()`. The source-grounded trigger established here is only that the selected glyph's CFF2 charstring reaches `OpCode_blendcs` with a nonzero cached region count `k` and fewer than `(k + 1) * n` operands remaining after `n = env.argStack.pop_uint()`, so line 239 underflows `start` and line 241 passes an out-of-range `BlendArg` slice into `set_blends()`. The staged artifacts do not expose the exact numeric `n` and `k` values in this witness or justify a broader trigger class than fonts reproducing this same underflow relation.
